title: simple_tank_keep_direction
description:
differential (tank) steering that feels exactly like a normal tank mix - full STEERING stick spins the machine continuously, there is no 360 or 180 degree dial to aim - but the instant the stick returns to centre, the heading it stopped at is held against drift by the catalogue's own 'PID' block, running every pass.

HOW: the stick does not set an angle, it sets a TURN RATE. p5 (integrator) integrates STEERING every pass into an unbounded virtual accumulator - hold the stick and it counts up forever, exactly like the machine itself would keep turning. p6 divides that down into a virtual TARGET HEADING (raw_div_lit k, default 500: smaller = faster spin per stick deflection, at full stick this is about 2000 angle units/sec, ~0.5 turn/sec - kept modest on purpose, see the wrap note below). p7 is the REAL heading from the IMU. p8-p14 take target minus real heading and wrap it the SHORT way round the turn (-2048..+2047, never the long way), because the target can be millions of units away after a few turns and only the remainder matters. p14b clamps that to +-1024 as a hard safety margin before it ever reaches the PID. p15 is the 'PID' block: sp = that clamped, wrapped error, pv = 0 (so its internal 'sp - pv' IS the error), out = the steering value actually used by the tank differential math below (p16 onward, same diff-redistribution as the 'simple tank' preset).

When the stick is centred the virtual target stops moving (integrator input is 0) and the PID fights any real drift back to it - true heading hold, always running, never switched off. When the stick moves the target races ahead and the PID chases it, which is what gives the stick authority: it is driving a rate command into the same loop that holds you still when you let go.

WHY p14b AND kd=0 EXIST - a real bug found and fixed in an earlier version: the 'PID' block computes its D term as (error - previous error) / dt, with dt in milliseconds. Because p14's error is a WRAPPED angle, it can jump discontinuously by up to ~4095 units in a single 1 ms pass whenever the virtual target's lead over the real heading crosses 180 degrees (which happens if the commanded turn rate outruns how fast the chassis can actually turn). Divided by a ~1 ms dt, that jump became a spurious value in the hundreds of thousands, slammed the output to its rail, and the same jump also put a lasting kick into the integral accumulator - which is exactly what 'turns fine one way, spins flat out and stays there the other way' looks like: whichever direction happened to build up that much lag during testing hit it, the other did not. kd is 0 here because a derivative of a signal that can wrap is not well behaved at the wrap point, full stop; p14b's +-1024 clamp is a second, independent guard so even a large true lag is never handed to the PID as a value anywhere near the +-2048 discontinuity; and p6's default was slowed down so the commanded rate stays comfortably below what this preset's default chassis (track 14 cm, 120 cm/s wheels) can actually achieve, which keeps real lag small in the first place.

TUNE ON THE REAL MACHINE:
- p15 kp/ki (x1000 fixed point, defaults 600/50): if the robot turns away from the target instead of toward it, negate kp and ki together - the sign is set by which way positive steering turns YOUR chassis, which this tool cannot know in advance.
- p15 ilo/ihi (anti-windup, default +-500000): lower it if the robot overshoots badly after a big stick move.
- p6's k (default 500): lower for a snappier spin at full stick, but keep it slow enough that the chassis can actually keep up - if it cannot, raise p14b's clamp instead of fighting it with a faster kd, since re-adding kd on a wrapped signal reopens the bug above.
- p5's anti-windup (+-2,000,000,000) is deliberately close to int32 range - it is meant to never actually bind; the machine would have to hold full stick turning for a very long time to reach it.

Requires firmware 2.1.0+ (the levelled IMU / imu_heading and PID blocks) and an armed, calibrated IMU - see the Robot tab and README_MIX_EDITOR_API.md 8.1.

nodes.name: zero
nodes.note: reused wherever a RAW zero or an always-false gate is needed.

nodes.name: always false
nodes.note: the integrator below needs its reset port wired to something - this never fires, the accumulator only clears on a disarm gap (onResume).

nodes.name: steering integral (virtual, unbounded)
nodes.note: sums the stick every pass, exactly like the real machine keeps turning while you hold it. The bound is deliberately near int32 range so it never actually binds in normal use.

nodes.name: target heading (virtual)
nodes.note: smaller k = faster spin per stick deflection, but keep it slow enough the chassis can actually keep up - see the description's note on why kd is 0.

nodes.name: current heading
nodes.note: reset port intentionally left unwired: only the stick's own integral moves the target, the IMU reading itself is never forced back to zero.

nodes.name: heading error, signed (short way)
nodes.note: the short way round the turn, -2048..+2047 - never the long way, however many laps the virtual target is ahead.

nodes.name: error, capped (safety)
nodes.note: a second, independent guard so the PID never sees a value anywhere near the +-2048 wrap discontinuity, whatever the true lag is. See the description for the bug this closes.

nodes.name: heading PID
nodes.note: sp = the capped, wrapped error, pv = 0, so its internal (sp - pv) IS the error. Output is the steering value used by the tank math below - the pilot never touches the wheels directly. Flip kp and ki together if the robot corrects the wrong way. kd is deliberately 0 - see the description.
